txt: A man is sleeping at the table, wearing mud-caked boots and rolled down overalls. The back of his shirt reads "WILD PINES", encircled by a logo with a tree.
He rubs his face, before burying it in his hands. You can hear a faint snore.
It's a dockworker's ID, doubling as a shift card and a job permit. A young, able-bodied man stares back at you from the photo: Santiago S. John.
On the counter -- rolled out of his open hand -- you see a blister pack of headache medicine.
The dockworker doesn't answer, his head is already back down on the table. In sweet sleep.
The man does not mind. You probably need them more than he does.
The man emits a loud snore. Is he about to wake up? Doesn't look like it, but you never know. Better be quick!
The sleeping dockworker has little to say about your actions. He remains silent.
The worker is in a deep slumber.
The worker stares at you, his eyes dry from sleep. A web of wrinkles covers his tanned forehead.
"Brilliant." The worker blinks, as if trying to scare away the sleep.
"Congratulations, you have seen the future. Now if you excuse me again, officer..." The worker sinks back onto the table, ready to continue his nap.
"Everyone. It's a local rumour." He yawns suddenly.
"For one -- I could get some god damn shut-eye." He rubs his eyes, then lets his head fall back on the table. "Right to *sleep*, I say."
"For one -- I could use some more shut-eye in the mornings..." He rubs his eyes and sighs. "Right to work? Right to *sleep*, I say."
"Good, then you understand the gist of it. We would all be better off without the employers and their employment."
"Good." He doesn't dwell on the particulars of your existence. "We're in the middle of a strike down at the harbour. Trying to force some sense into the executive board of Wild Pines."
"Haven't you noticed what's going on outside?"
"How's it going?" The dockworker lets out a big yawn, then stares at the cafeteria's terrace doors. Some fingerprints glisten on the glass.
"I can tell you this -- trouble's ahead."
"I don't know what you're talking about, kind sir, but when I'm out, then I'm really *out*. No corpses. No mausoleums. Just *quality-time*."
"I don't know what you're talking about, kind sir, but when I'm out, then I'm really *out*. No ex-anything. Just *quality time*."
"I don't know what you're talking about, kind sir, but when I'm out, then I'm really *out*. No malt grains or whatever. No poetry-stuff. Just *quality-time*."
"If someone has decided to die on top of a tree, then how is it my concern?"
"If you get lucky, I might even have answers for them."
"Indeed. Help yourself to some." He blinks. "Wait, no, it's empty. Sorry about that, pal."
"Knocks you right out when you drown a bottle or two." He rubs his face, then buries it in his hands. You can hear a faint snore.
"Logistics? No, it's a nightmare." He lets his head fall back on the table.
"Okay, I guess there's also Evrart, he's in charge of the Union. He's smart. Knows how to negotiate. He's got our back."
"Really? You woke me up for that?" The worker gives you a vacant stare, then groans. "Fine, what is it, officer?"
"Thank god, no."
"That's the name of my employer. I work in logistics."
"They got it. Measurehead's got it, he's guarding the gate. I'm just getting some sleep. Or *was*..."
"They say your guy was a killer. Your tree-man. He has friends, same as him. Killers. There's only one thing they know well -- how to wreak havoc."
"Wait, what? I was just sleeping." He seems pissed off. "What do you want, officer?"
"We are... the workers. The Union. We know what we need, what's right for us."
"We're in the middle of a strike down at the harbour. Trying to force some sense into the executive board of Wild Pines."
"Why the yelling, man?" The 30-something man slowly lifts his head and gives you a pensive look.
"Yeah, what about it?"
"You heard what I said. Draw your own conclusions. That's all I know, and I prefer to keep it this way."
"You know, people die here every day. Someone's found in a ditch, another one falls in a manhole, a third one gets eaten by stray dogs." He respites.
"Zzz...  zzzzz... zzz..."
"Zzzz..."
"Zzzzzzzz..."
